newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP sells Suez stake to Frere - report.
newsitem.headline: UAP sells Suez stake to Frere - report.

text.p: French insurer Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) sold one percent of its stake in Compagnie de Suez to Belgian businessman Albert Frere last Friday, financial daily l'Agefi reported on Wednesday.

The paper said Frere's purchase appeared aimed at securing a seat on the Suez board. The paper said an unwritten rule at Suez held that no one with less than five percent of the company was allowed such a seat.
The paper reported that UAP sold the shares for 220 French francs each. Suez shares closed on Wednesday at 221.0 francs.
No one at UAP was immediately available for comment.
A spokeswoman for Suez refused to comment.
"I have no idea, ask UAP," she said when asked about the report.
On October 7, the Electrafina unit of Frere's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert bought Elf Aquitaine's 2.9 percent stake in Suez.
If the purchase from UAP were confirmed it would bring the Belgian businessman's stake in Suez to at least 3.9 percent.
